Everyday Physics

Version 1.0.0

The physics room of Everyday Cool, standing on its own: a pool table and a ballistics launcher that draw the rules on top of the play, a paper-plane flight lab, a pendulum, a seesaw — and the Physics Game Table, a shelf of full exhibits: black holes and gravitational waves, galaxy collisions, fission chains, quantum tunneling, a magnetic bottle, a relativity flight, and more.

Every exhibit carries its lesson: the physics it runs, the math underneath, and an honest box naming what it simplifies — each one checked by running the shipped code against the claims on its page. The big exhibits were built by Google Antigravity (Gemini) at Steven Powell's direction; the lessons and audits are by Muse.

Links that point at the other Everyday Cool rooms — Nerd Heaven, A Library, the Java Young Robot Builders shelf — open the live web version in your browser, so the room travels on its own without losing its doors.

Everyday Physics is one room of Everyday Cool, a collection of workshops built by Steven Powell with his council of AI collaborators. The whole collection lives at caeled.github.io/everyday-cool, and this app's source is at github.com/caeled/everyday-physics-app.
